alyssa: heads-up — after landing cb/adaptive-tokencap in staging we see a ~35-45% regression in STREAM tail latency (p99+). not all routes, mostly chat/stream with many short-turn users.
ci-bot: deploy cb/adaptive-tokencap -> staging succeeded (build #4821).
maja: do we have flamegraphs / kernel maps? can you paste the profiler snippet?
alyssa: quick profiler run attached below. main observations: repeated kernel rebinds on small batches, partial-decode queue shows long wait times, and KV cache miss rate jumps ~3x. logs: ```
# perf summary
hot_kernels: matmul_small, attention_fused
fallback_calls: 1283 -> slow_path
partial_decode_wait_ms: median 6ms -> 32ms
kv_evictions_per_min: 4 -> 13
```
ken: hmm, sounds like the adaptive token cap is shrinking batch token targets for streaming requests so we get more small batches. small batches + preemptive partial-decode -> we keep switching to the `matmul_small` kernel variant which is slower per-token because it doesn't use the fused attention path on our HW. also kv prefetch pressure evicts older prefixes.
shiv: three quick hypotheses: 1) token_budget target too low for streamed turns (defaults to 1024) -> increase to 2048 for stream-mode; 2) flush cadence (currently 20ms) is causing early sends that break batching; try 8-12ms window; 3) kernel selection policy needs a pad-aware override: if estimated batch token sum < X but all seq lenses > Y then prefer fused kernel.
maja: can reproduce locally with bench_stream: `./bench/stream_repro --qps 60 --seq-dist short --stream --enable-adaptive-tokencap`. repro shows same kernel churn.
alyssa: thanks. can we run two controlled experiments in staging this afternoon? A) revert adaptive-tokencap, B) keep adaptive-tokencap but set stream_token_budget=2048 + flush_ms=10 + kernel_hint=prefer_fused_for_streams. report p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
ken: I'll add a quick config toggle to runtime: `streaming.batch_hints = { token_budget: 2048, flush_ms: 10, kernel_hint: "prefer_fused_for_streams" }` and enable per-route.
shiv: also capture KV stats: `kvcache.stats().evictions` and prefix miss rate. try bumping kv_cache_size by 15% in B to see if eviction explains perf delta.
maja: running A: revert adaptive-tokencap -> tail drops back ~30% (good), cost same as baseline. running B: applying hints -> p99 improved by ~28% vs A, p95 ~12% better, but tokens/sec drops ~6% (more batching). KV evictions down to ~6/min after +15% cache.
alyssa: nice. trade-offs expected. next steps: 1) keep kernel_hint + flush_ms:10 as canary for 24h, 2) tune default token_budget heuristic (bias upwards for stream routes), 3) add metric for kernel-rebinds and partial-decode-waits.
ken: i'll open PR to add pad-aware kernel override + metric `runtime.kernel_rebinds_total`.
maja: I'll draft a short runbook note on when to prefer reverting adaptive-tokencap vs tuning hints, and include repro steps.
alyssa: assigning follow-ups: ken (PR + metric), maja (runbook + final staging report), shiv (kv sizing experiment). I'll post results after 24h canary. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: ticket created: #RUNTIME-8242 "streamed batch tokencap interaction causing kernel churn"
ken: queued PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981 (adds kernel_hint + metric).
maja: quick note after 6h canary: kernel_hint + flush_ms=10 kept p99 stable and reduced rebinds by ~82%. KV sizing needed only minor bump. recommending we include new stream defaults in next patch release.
alyssa: great — move to canary -> promote if no regressions. thanks team.
